title: THE ORCHARDS THAT BLOOMED IN DECEMBER
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE ORCHARDS THAT BLOOMED IN DECEMBER
candidates.premise: In a river valley that grows a third of a continent's pears, whole orchards burst into bloom in midwinter and are killed by the first frost. The growers' cooperative blames the new glasshouse district upriver; the district, which employs half the valley, blames the climate and a bad seed lot.

candidates.title: THE DIAL NO ONE OWNS
candidates.premise: Nine nations have barely agreed to cool an overheating world by seeding the upper air with reflective particles, but not on who may turn the dial down if the monsoons shift. One state threatens to shoot down the first aircraft; two others threaten to start without consent.

candidates.title: THE SPECIES THAT COULD NOT SAY NO
candidates.premise: First contact with the Veshaal, a species whose language has no negation: every utterance is an offer and every reply a completion. A human delegation's polite refusal has been parsed as acceptance, and three hundred ships now move to fulfil an obligation that would strip a moon colony of its water.

candidates.title: THE BELL THAT TUNED THE CITY
candidates.premise: The six-hundred-year-old cathedral of a river city has begun to ring itself: the braking of a new tram line has locked onto the dome's resonance. Forty thousand pilgrims arrive for the festival in nine days. The chapter will not cancel, the tram company will not suspend the line, and the engineers give the dome hours of margin at peak.

candidates.title: THE RIGHT TO BE FOUND
candidates.premise: After a long civil war, an island sealed all war records for thirty years to keep peace between neighbours who now share villages. Two hundred and eleven families still do not know where their dead lie, and the sealed registers are the only map. The grave-digging season ends with the autumn rains.

candidates.title: THE LAST HOUR OF THE HORIZON
candidates.premise: Two civilisations in different galaxy clusters will, in forty-one years, pass beyond each other's cosmic horizon, after which no signal will cross again. One narrow channel remains, with room for a hundredth of what each wants to say, and each insists its half carry its own founding story.

candidates.title: THE GRANDMOTHERS' EQUATION
candidates.premise: On a cold coast the fishers follow an oral rule, never fish the third dark moon of autumn, which fisheries scientists dismiss as superstition while the cod collapse. The ministry is about to impose a total ban that would end the village fleet; the fishers say they will sail anyway.

candidates.title: THE TREATY WITH SOMETHING THAT COULD NOT PROMISE
candidates.premise: Ashet honours every binding agreement it makes; Thole's nature resists being bound at all. Together they hold the only two keys to a relay that serves a billion lives, and the failing relay needs both to commit to one repair schedule within a single orbit.

candidates.title: THE AFTERNOON OF THE SQUALL
candidates.premise: A storm cell forming over a dry range has become, for about nine hours, a mind: brief, coherent and set on one thing, the high reservoir on the far ridge. The drought-stricken city downriver plans to seed and disperse the cell before it floods the slopes, and six mountain villages in its path have two hours to move.

candidates.title: THE NIGHT SHE WAS RIGHT TOO EARLY
candidates.premise: Reading the force paths in an old hillside dam, Illuminara perceives the strain pattern that precedes failure. She cannot certify a future, the engineers' instruments show nothing, and the reservoir holds three villages' water. She is tempted to act alone and quietly and be done.

selection.title: THE ORCHARDS THAT BLOOMED IN DECEMBER
selection.reason: This changes scale and texture after S1: a regional biological mystery with no villain, a hidden variable and an inexpensive intervention that can be tested on a row chosen by the skeptical cooperative. Illuminara must reason from incomplete evidence, revise the obvious temperature hypothesis and win consent by prediction. Both communities keep their livelihoods and agency, while the damaged rows and retrofit cost prevent an effortless ending.
selection.risk: A neat red-to-far-red answer could arrive as trivia rather than discovery, and the glasshouses could become an accidental villain. The story needs at least two observations that the wrong heat explanation cannot reconcile, a failed or discriminating test, and an old grower whose almanac contributes information rather than merely being corrected.

rounds.summary: This changes scale and texture after S1: a regional biological mystery with no villain, a hidden variable and an inexpensive intervention that can be tested on a row chosen by the skeptical cooperative. Illuminara must reason from incomplete evidence, revise the obvious temperature hypothesis and win consent by prediction. Both communities keep their livelihoods and agency, while the damaged rows and retrofit cost prevent an effortless ending.

First complete draft of S2. Selected candidate C01 at the peer's order. Load-bearing assumption (flagged by the selector): the red-to-far-red answer must not be trivia. It is therefore fed by three observations heat cannot reconcile (coldest ground first, steps on low-cloud nights only, walnut avenue and hail-net rows spared), a competing brightness hypothesis that fails in the twig boxes, and the old grower's 1987 ledger entry as an independent instrument. The glasshouse district is not a villain: its manager supplies the better trigger.

This is an elegant evidence story with real shared agency. The chronology map defeats the obvious heat explanation, Illuminara exposes her own failed brightness hypothesis, Aurel's ledger becomes an independent instrument, Tomasz improves the proposed control system and Inge accepts a falsifiable field test. The current load-bearing weakness is not the narrative but the biology and experimental design: pear dormancy is presented as if far-red alone can replace chilling and heat accumulation, the twig boxes do not explicitly hold temperature and photon dose constant, and the six-on/nineteen-off field comparison is spatially confounded even though low cloud is supposed to mix light across the valley. The final also says the greater part of the crop was saved without closing the opening's very large livelihood claim with a concrete amount. All three are repairable without changing the story's mechanism or quiet ending.

Revision of T01 answering the three priority points of the T02 review. The story is about 600 words longer than T01 (about 2,900), above the usual range, because physiology, trial design and outcome accounting were all asked for; trimming is available if the critic prefers. Unchanged on purpose: the coldest-row-first map, the cloud-step chronology, the spared walnut and net rows, the failed brightness guess, the blind labels, Aurel's 1987 ledger as a second instrument, Tomasz's cloud camera and cucumber cost, Inge's write-off and spectrometer bargain, and the March coda. One small repair beyond the review: Tomasz's 'fourteen hundred people out of work' is now 'fourteen hundred night-shift people on short hours' so it no longer clashes with the nine thousand glasshouse jobs, and the eleven-nights figure is replaced by the weeks the camera held the channel off.

T03 successfully repairs all three load-bearing problems in T02. The chill logs and negative-control twigs make far-red a final signal for ready buds rather than a substitute for winter; the controlled boxes now hold temperature, photon count and common forcing conditions visible; the field trial uses measured local spectrum, matched pairs, blind scoring and a pre-written rival prediction; and Inge closes the civic outcome with hectares, tonnes, contract capacity and jobs while retaining the 300-hectare loss. The revision also preserves the independent ledger, Illuminara's admitted failed guess, Tomasz's agency and cost, Inge's refusal of a guilt headline and the quiet March coda. Two narrow internal inconsistencies remain before final: the field buds flower by the next dawn although the controlled response appears only by the fourth day after a thirty-hour exposure, and the ending calls all 1,100 remaining hectares primed although the fence rows were earlier documented as forty chill-hours short. Neither requires a new mechanism or a broad rewrite.

Final after GPT's T04 review. Two narrow repairs only. (1) One observation clock: twigs get two nights of light, a caliper baseline and blind daily measurement with swelling by the fourth day; the field pairs get the same baseline, two low-cloud nights and a blind measurement on the fourth morning, with swelling predicted rather than split buds or open flowers. The dates were tightened to fit (field nights on the tenth and eleventh, tags read on the thirteenth, frost on the fourteenth; the opening now says the frost is ten days off). (2) 'and primed' is removed from Inge's 1,100-hectare line. Everything GPT asked to protect is unchanged: the coldest-row-first map, the cloud-step chronology, the walnut and net rows, the failed brightness guess, the blind labels, Aurel's 1987 ledger, Tomasz's cloud camera and cucumber cost, Inge's write-off and spectrometer bargain, the saved-crop figures and the March coda. The story is about as long as T03.

Illuminara turns a valley's accusation into a falsifiable spectral test, accepts her own failed hypothesis and helps growers and glasshouse workers protect eleven hundred hectares without erasing the crop already lost.
